result.title: Learning to Formalize: Bridging Open-Ended Workloads and Fast Decision Models
result.comment: 10 pages, 2 figures, only for concept verification now
result.summary: Decision models offer fast choices over sup- plied alternatives, while general-purpose large language models interpret open-ended tasks through flexible generation and reasoning at the cost of sequential decoding. Many work- loads expect a generative backend to determine what can be done and therefore provide no well-defined candidate list. We bridge this in- terface gap with a small candidate formalizer trained on offline teacher-generated lists. The formalizer constructs explicit, validated alter- natives from task context, and a frozen deci- sion model selects an entry. A motivating com- parison with official TypeSafe Jev-1.13.0 on 200 CALVIN-D test episodes reports 11% suc- cess with generic motions versus 46.5% with DeepSeek V4 Flash pose candidates. Sepa- rately, a six-arm privileged-state evaluation on 1,011 CALVIN-D validation annotations finds that a locally deployed decision model can achieve at most 52.6% task success rate with the fine-tuned formalizer, compared with 11.8% without it, and the end-to-end latency is kept to 2.09 s, whereas Qwen3.5-27B is 3.67 s with the exact experiment setting.

AI.brief_summary: 论文针对开放式机器人任务（CALVIN-D）缺少候选列表的问题，训练一个小的候选形式化器，从任务上下文构造经过验证的备选项，再由冻结的快速决策模型从中选择，并报告成功率与端到端时延的概念验证结果。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「候选构造器 + 冻结轻量选择器」的两段式接口，可作为 latent 假设生成与廉价验证/筛选分工的参照，且时延对比可供核查 THINK/LOOK/STOP 的算力成本，但原文属机器人决策应用，状态与证据是否涉及视觉推理内部机制需读正文确认。
